entries.test: Public investment, acquisition and infrastructure records would show whether AI companies were becoming increasingly dependent on the named large technology companies by August 2024.
entries.note: The following sentences give the centralization claim a concrete financial meaning.

entries.test: Contemporaneous public statements or reporting from prospective GPT-5 customers would show whether they expected no significant improvement over GPT-4.
entries.note: The customer-expectations assertion is checkable; near-term delivery is presented only as a possibility.
This selects the indicator readers should prioritize rather than independently predicting its occurrence.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and fundraising records after August 2024 would show whether both companies required billions in fresh financing soon and whether other AI companies could raise if they could not.
entries.note: “Nobody” refers contextually to other AI companies. The record combines a funding forecast with a conditional industry-wide claim.
The prediction depends on desperation and attributes a private purpose to a future demonstration. A public launch alone would not establish those elements.

entries.test: Public launch-schedule records and Sora revenue and cost disclosures would show whether an accelerated release produced an unprofitable product.
entries.note: The profitability assertion is categorical. Relative operating cost and entertaining failures are separately hedged.
“Could be eliminated” states a possibility. “Such as” turns his specification of the needed breakthrough into merely an example.

entries.test: Public financing records would show whether continuation of the boom required billions in additional cloud-company commitments and further funding for OpenAI and Anthropic.
entries.note: This asserts necessary future financing conditions, rather than simply describing current finances.

entries.test: Financial disclosures and public shareholder demands would show whether generative AI became a financial burden and generated pressure to reduce investment and capital expenditure.
entries.note: The next sentence makes the financial meaning of “albatross” clear. He also expressly predicts that the antecedent will occur.
A chance of another round and difficulty imagining survival do not commit him to a definite outcome.

entries.test: Public transaction and operating records following an OpenAI or Anthropic collapse would show whether a large technology company absorbed it through a Character.ai-style arrangement.
entries.note: The absorption prediction is firm conditional on collapse. Shutdown probability and the attributed concealment motive are not independently settled by that test.
“If I had to guess” and “most likely” explicitly qualify the proposed acquirer.
The record attributes private motives, and “another con” supplies no agreed criterion for a future venture. The three-year horizon ends August 5, 2027.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and documented deployments available by August 2024 would show whether generative AI could automate spreadsheet and document drudgery or provide the described personalized assistance.
entries.note: The preceding sentence supplies the referents. The automation denial has a concrete plain reading.
The surrounding denunciation and his express concessions about useful document processing mark “not helping anybody” as hyperbole.

entries.test: Public financing, capital-expenditure and corporate survival records would show whether generative AI funding dried up and the boom collapsed under his stated definition.
entries.note: “Seems inevitable” expresses a firm expectation in context. Earlier paragraphs explicitly define collapse.

entries.test: Publicly documented GPT-5 training runs, compute access and architecture disclosures would show whether OpenAI lacked the chips and a new architecture at publication.
entries.note: The principal assertions concern existing resources. GPT-5's anticipated impact is a separate probabilistic forecast.
“Maybe six months” qualifies the available runway rather than establishing a firm deadline.

entries.test: Public product-level financial disclosures would show whether OpenAI's SearchGPT search offering ever became profitable.
entries.note: “I don't think you're gonna” expresses a negative expectation here, rather than merely a possibility.
“Can't imagine” expresses incredulity rather than a firm prediction about purchases or advertising.

entries.test: After hyperscalers withdraw, public product and deployment records would show whether a modest form of generative AI remains in operation.
entries.note: “Fully believe” is firm expectation. The antecedent is hyperscaler withdrawal, with no deadline.
